scope: Every date, clock and MW value in 40 distinct complete CSV bodies compared independently with csv.reader; duplicate byte-identical bodies reused across seven archives are recorded separately. Hypothetical solar workbooks compared with openpyxl, including all embedded site metadata. Values use source numeric precision as exposed by openpyxl; no XML-decimal exactness claim.

sourceDetails: An ERCOT_onshore_2011.CSV row contains a 2011 onshore table and a separately dated 2013 offshore table; sourceBlock preserves their identity.
Six final rows in that file have an empty, shortened offshore block. No offshore records are synthesized.
Original source records are preserved; totals do not count unique site/timestamp observations across overlapping tables and publications.
remainingFormats: The two older existing/hypothetical wind-shape workbook layouts are not yet supported. Their four linked URLs resolve to two distinct cached workbook ZIP contents.
The oldest solar shapes have Date (MM/DD), Time (HH:MM), weather-year columns and TMY3; their units and non-calendar-year representation require separate handling.
Fifteen of the nineteen newer profile workbooks remain unverified; discovery alone is not evidence of parsing or complete retention.
